summary: Describes base requirements for the Pseudo-Wire Emulation Edge to Edge working group. It guides other documents that define mechanisms for emulating Ethernet, ATM and Frame Relay over packet networks.

eli5.summary: It makes a packet network act like a dedicated wire between two places. This document lists what the pretend wire must be able to do.

questions: what does a provider edge device do
subtitle: What a pseudo-wire must do to make a packet network pass for a dedicated Ethernet, ATM or Frame Relay circuit.

tldr.problem: Service providers ran separate overlay networks for services such as Frame Relay and Internet access, which was expensive. They wanted one packet network that still carried the older services.
tldr.mechanism: Pseudo-wire emulation edge-to-edge (PWE3) wraps each service's frames and carries them across a packet switched network between two provider edge devices. This document lists the requirements any such mechanism must meet for encapsulation, maintenance, management and faithfulness.
tldr.outcome: It guides the working group's later documents for Ethernet, ATM and Frame Relay. It is informational and standardizes no protocol itself.

facts.label: ATM and Frame Relay checksum
facts.value: Removed at ingress PE, recalculated at egress PE

today: RFC 3916 is an Informational document, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It sets requirements for the working group's service-specific documents and does not itself define a protocol.

sections.title: Why Emulate a Wire
sections.content:
A pseudo wire (PW) emulates the essential attributes of a service such as ATM, Frame Relay or Ethernet over a Packet Switched Network (PSN). It encapsulates service-specific data units arriving at an ingress port, carries them across a path or tunnel, and manages their timing and order so the behavior of the service is reproduced as faithfully as possible. To the customer, the PW looks like an unshared link or circuit of the chosen service.

The motivation is economic. A provider delivering several services usually runs parallel overlay networks, one per service, which is expensive in capital and operating cost. The RFC notes that Frame Relay currently earns more revenue per bit than native IP, and private line TDM earns more still, and that a lot of legacy equipment does not speak IP. Emulation lets those services ride on a single IP-optimized core.

The RFC also gives four questions for deciding whether an application suits PWE3: is it deployed widely enough, do providers want it, do equipment makers want it, and are the savings worth the complexity and limitations. All four need a yes.
sections.eli5: A company that runs many separate roads for many kinds of trucks would rather build one big road. A pseudo-wire lets the old trucks keep driving as if they still had their own road.

sections.title: The Reference Model
sections.content:
A PW is a connection between two provider edge (PE) devices that joins two attachment circuits (ACs). An AC can be a Frame Relay DLCI, an ATM VPI/VCI, an Ethernet port, a VLAN, a HDLC link, a PPP connection, a PPP session from an L2TP tunnel, an MPLS LSP, and so on. The customer devices at the far ends are customer edge (CE) devices, and a CE is not aware that it is using an emulated service rather than a native one.

During PW setup the two PEs are configured, or automatically exchange information, about the service to be emulated. After that, a frame received from an AC is encapsulated and sent over the PW, and the remote PE rebuilds the native frame and forwards it to the other CE. One or more PWs can be carried inside a PSN tunnel.

The document does not assume a particular kind of PW (it names L2TPv3 sessions and MPLS LSPs as examples) or a particular PSN (IP or MPLS). The requirements are generic and apply to Ethernet, ATM, Frame Relay and other services.
sections.eli5: Each end has a mailroom (the provider edge) that packs the customer's package, sends it across town in a delivery truck, and unpacks it on the other side so it looks untouched.

sections.title: Packet Processing Requirements
sections.content:
Every PE MUST provide an encapsulation mechanism for the data units from an AC, and every PWE3 service MUST specify what that data unit is. The mechanism must convey the L2 header information the egress needs, accommodate variable length units when the native service allows them, and, where a service can group circuits into a trunk, carry enough information to demultiplex the individual circuits. Some information, such as the service type, can be kept as state at the egress during setup instead of in each packet.

Every service must also say whether a frame checksum is preserved across the PW or removed at the ingress PE and recalculated at the egress PE. For ATM and Frame Relay the checksum covers link-local circuit identifiers, so it MUST be removed and recalculated.

Three more concerns are handled per service. If order matters, a mechanism MUST ensure in-order delivery, for example a sequence number in the PW header. If duplicates are not allowed, a mechanism MUST prevent them. If payload plus headers exceeds the path MTU, each service document MUST say whether to fragment or drop, and fragmentation is best avoided because of its performance cost. For small payloads, several may be concatenated under one PSN tunnel header, with each keeping its own PW header, weighed against added delay and jitter.
sections.eli5: Every package needs a label saying what it is and where it goes. If packages must arrive in order, they get numbers, and if a box is too big for the truck, the rules say whether to cut it up or leave it behind.

sections.title: Maintenance and Management
sections.content:
Every PWE3 approach MUST define a setup mechanism so the PEs can exchange what they need, such as encapsulation and ordering methods. Setup and teardown can be triggered by a PE management command, by setup or teardown of an AC, or by auto-discovery, and manual configuration counts as a special kind of signaling. A bidirectional emulated circuit can be signaled Up only when the PW and PSN tunnels work in both directions.

In-band maintenance messages of the native service, such as ATM OAM and Frame Relay LMI, SHOULD simply be carried through the PW without translation. Out-of-band messages must have their handling specified by each emulated service. PEs also must initiate maintenance messages themselves when a PW or an AC link fails, because the CEs would otherwise get no link failure notification, and such messages MUST be native messages of the service so the CEs stay unaware of the emulation.

For management, SNMP MIBs MUST be provided for each emulated circuit and for the PW. They MUST augment or extend existing MIB tables rather than redefine them, an AC MUST appear as an interface in the ifTable, and the MIBs MUST collect statistics for performance and fault management. A connection verification mechanism and a traceroute function SHOULD be supported.
sections.eli5: If the string between the tin cans breaks, the cans cannot feel it. So the mailrooms must send a warning message that both customers understand, using the same kind of message they would have used with a real string.

sections.title: Faithfulness, QoS and Non-Requirements
sections.content:
An emulated service SHOULD be as similar to the native service as possible, but is not required to be identical, and each service's applicability statement MUST report its limitations. Four things MUST hold: type, speed and MTU can be defined for the emulated circuit if they can be for a native one; the circuit appears unshared to each CE even when PWs share physical paths; both CEs are notified in a timely manner if the circuit fails, where the native service would notify them; and a routing protocol adjacency that works over a native circuit works over an emulated one.

Service quality does not have to match the native service. The working group defines mechanisms for emulation, not the services, and the quality to offer is a matter between a provider and its customers. QoS is still important, and the RFC says operators may rely on over-provisioning or deploy QoS mechanisms. PWE3 may not suit services with severe delay or jitter constraints.

Out of scope are service interworking, selecting a particular type of PW, making emulation perfectly match the native service, signaling PSN tunnels, traffic management of PW packets, and any multicast service that is not native to the emulated medium.
sections.eli5: The pretend string does not have to be exactly like the real one, but it has to act enough like it that the people on the cans do not notice. Some jobs, like very fast games of catch, may not work well.

sections.title: Inter-Domain Use and Security
sections.content:
A PW is a matter between its end-points and is transparent to the devices in between, so inter-domain PWE is fundamentally similar to intra-domain PWE as long as both ends use the same approach. Security may matter more across domains, where end-point authentication MAY be applied, and QoS gets harder because one provider cannot control another's traffic management. Providers have to cooperate and agree on high quality of service for certain traffic. Setting up inter-domain PSN tunnels is harder, but that is an issue for tunneling protocols such as MPLS and L2TPv3 and is outside PWE3.

For security, the PW end-point, the PW demultiplexing mechanism and the payloads can all be attacked. PWE3 should use the security mechanisms of the PW demultiplexer or PSN layers, which SHOULD protect against denial-of-service attacks and spoofing of native data units and of tunneled PW data. Validating traffic addressed to the PW demultiplexer end-point is called paramount, and IPsec is named as one usable security protocol.
sections.eli5: If the string crosses a neighbor's yard, the neighbor has to agree to help. And someone must make sure nobody can slip a fake note into the cans.

viz.caption: THE PARTS OF THE PWE3 REFERENCE MODEL

items.title: CE
items.text: Customer edge device where a service starts or ends. It does not know the service is emulated.

items.title: PE
items.text: Provider edge device that provides PWE3 to a CE.

items.title: AC
items.text: Attachment circuit joining a CE to a PE, such as a DLCI, VPI/VCI, Ethernet port or VLAN.

items.title: PW
items.text: Pseudo wire carrying the essential elements of the circuit from one PE to the other.

items.title: PSN tunnel
items.text: Tunnel across the packet network inside which one or more PWs travel.
